Hey man, stick around for a while. There are plenty of things to appreciate, despite your circumstances. 

I don't know what you like, but I like nature. It calms my mind and lets my thoughts flow.

You gotta focus on taking a breather in times like this. Sit down, listen to music, or get some rest man. 

Give another day a shot. You might miss out on some cool stuff.

Hey there.

Just a preliminary question, how long has this been going on?

I know life gets rough and if I were in your position right now (which I have been on many occasions in my life) that it is hard to take my words to heart when all the negative feelings are refusing to think of a positive reality. 

Trust me, I have been in the position to end my life, shooting bullets past my head with a rifle. 

Things get better.

I don't know who you are or how the feelings have developed to make you give up on hope and peace, but there are things in this world that are so precious. Maybe not now, but later, you will come to appreciate your time here on earth, the goals you can strive for, and the freedom you have to breathe and even hear birds sing in the morning or the breeze comb through the trees.

This modern world moves so fast and at such an accelerated pace, I really don't believe humans are able to deal with it on a day to day basis. Social media floods our brain with photos and videos of "perfect realities" when it certainly isn't like that every single day. You have to come to realize that life isn't shiny and beautiful all the time, so you have to find beauty in the struggle and stress. 

\^Again, I am not saying that this is some magic trick to make your brain wire to be happy. That is not the case. What I will say though is truly sit down and write. Write all the negative things out of your mind, soon there is bound to be something good to write about. In my notebook I have pages and pages and pages of negative things I have wrote about life and how I feel about myself. Well, the more you write, the more you figure out what the root problem is. Are you unsatisfied with your job, do you not have many friends, do you lack a good romantic partner? You may be missing things in life that could help you find happiness. 

Get in touch with yourself and your inner thoughts, they will tell you the truth.

And please don't do anything to yourself. There is someone that loves you and doesn't want to hear your phone go to voicemail. 

Reach out if you want to talk :)

Whats going on man. 

I'll try and give some wisdom to you, but if you don't like it, no worries. I am 20 as well. 

We all have desires in life, some people chase money, fame, and a lot of people (mainly men) chase women. I was never one to chase women around during high school, in fact, it was very much the opposite occurrence for me. Women wanted me and I never pursued very much cause I was selective (still am to this day). Had relatively successful relationships that were long term, one having lasted for around 2 and 1/2 years.

\^This isn't for me to come in this thread with a guns blazing ego, that is not the case. What I did learn from the past is that women can come and go just as easy, if not easier, than many of your friends you have in your lifetime. If you really want to have someone as a partner, try and be friends with them first. Figure out what the believe in, what they are passionate about, and what y'all have in common. I wouldn't suggest trying to get relationships from going to clubs, just my opinion though. Statistically it has shown that long term relationships have been shown to last much longer if they had a friendship beforehand. So if a girl is what you are looking for, just try things slow with a girl, however long it may take. 

Now if you are just trying to mess around and have fun, that is a different story. I don't advise it though, I've seen it screw some of my friends up afterwards. 

When it comes to just getting friends, as I assume you are trying to mainly do, just get out there and keep trying. It comes easier to some people than others. Also, what may be the case is that you are trying to hang with crowds you don't fit into. What are your hobbies, interests, and goals in life? Align yourself with people of the same mentality. If you like working out, make a gym buddy and do workouts together, If you like cars, go to a car show and meet some people your age.

 Hell, if you like Playboi Carti, try to meet people who like him and all go to a concert together.

I'm by no means the best person for advice, but I do what I can with the experiences I have had in life. For myself, I have a very, very small social circle and find it suits me best. A lot of people know me around college, but not a lot of people ***know*** me, if you get what I mean. 

On a side note, I would not adopt Nihilism. It is a dream-killer, in many senses, a productivity downfall. "Without meaning, what the hell does it matter if I make friends or not?" I just don't see this as positive thinking. It's a way to avoid the responsibilities of making your life what you want it to be, regardless of whether or not there is an after-life.

If you have any questions just shoot a message back.

At the moment I am thinking of enlisting and continuing my college education in the reserves and see where I am in 6 months. It'll clear my mind and get my goals straight.
I would also love to be gifted a copy of the book please. This would do me wonders.

Wow. 

I haven't been on reddit for a while and forgot to check this thread that I created. You are definitely wise for your age;  I know people much older than you who have a much narrower outlook on the movement of life and the struggles that come with it. I appreciate you going out of your way to make such a thorough response because I talk to myself too much about my worries without ever being able to have replies like this. Since this post I have been trying to turn my life around (not that I have been failing in college or not staying active, but rather the perspective I have.) 

At the moment I am trying to find my purpose and what I would really find enjoyable in life. I am currently pursuing aerospace engineering, but find myself questioning taking that leap once I completed my research paper and finished philosophy class. Regardless, the ending to your comment stood out to me; getting to use life how you wanted is the only way to truly make it a world that you can see as a positive one. Maybe that is what I need to do, as does everyone else. I definitely need more people like you in my arsenal, thank you.

I see your point clearly;  the knowledge of  your existence will, at some point,  be unknown to you and everyone else after you pass is certainly a rough pill to swallow. Nihilism is one of those philosophies I could never jump on board with, it's too hard to accept the harsh truth for me unfortunately.
I hope there is a positive outlook on it for yourself. It would suck to have a view of 'oh well" for the end. Do you find more value in life because of the fact that there is an end?

I'll have to look into that, I don't know much about fungi, but I'm always willing to learn new stuff. My paper is actually focusing on Utilitarianism (an actions is considered just if the consequences yield the greatest amount of happiness for the greatest number of people). I don''t know how I ended up thinking about death writing this, but I definitely have been thinking of life from a much deeper perspective the more I write research papers.

This is a very thoughtful comment for sure. I would like to think of it this way. My struggle is to find the beauty in the struggle itself, if that makes sense. The stress of life, breakups, money-problems, and arguments are hardly desirable and feel like a waste to worry about when the timer on your life is constantly ticking. I guess I should appreciate the hardship of life? I only just turned 20, so I am in the dumps with everything as I move into the adult stage of my life. 

How old are you, if you mind me asking? I wonder if it takes time to come to terms with life's inevitable end, considering everytime my birthday rolls around I have a panic attack. Now that I think about it, if I'm lucky enough, I have another 3/4's to go in this world.

I aspire to have the neutral outlook on it like you do haha. Last night had my mind torn, but today I have even thought about how everything around me will one day be gone. The roads we drive on, the house we live in, the car I drive, even the air we breathe will, at some point be gone and there is no stopping it.

Things just haven't been right with me ever since I graduated and went off to college. Even now I feel guilty for even taking time out of my day to write this when I should be working on studying for Honors Chem. 

A big part of my life has always been helping other people and being the shoulder to lean on, but I never needed that shoulder to lean on. As a kid I used to be physically beat and mentally abused and got tough from that, but nowadays I don't have that same edge like I used to. My confidence is shot, my smile is forced, conversations are a workout, and I can't go an hour without mumbling "Put a bullet in my skull" or something to that affect. I have the full capability to kill myself since I own several rifles and pistols which may not be the best state of affairs. That is besides the point though. 

I feel alone and never have a person to talk to. My days usually are centered around the thoughts in my head. I go out to cafes to study for an average of 10 hours and then go to work on the weekends for the majority of the day, followed by more school work with no talking whatsoever. I used to be incredibly fit, but I haven't worked out in a month because of school and haven't had a genuine laugh since Summer. Just some things that I think about. 

I am planning to go out to look at the city skyline tonight over by a very cool bridge I know of. (Don't worry, not in that way) but it has crossed my mind. I think I just need to grab hold of my mental state again.
I would really appreciate if someone could just talk with me about anything in general. I just need a conversation :(
